subject: Culture
title: Eye Contact Wars
description: A micro-lesson that makes Eye Contact Wars usable.

hook.text: Americans read a dropped gaze as dishonest. Japanese people read a direct stare as hostile.

buildup.text: Western cultures link eye contact to confidence. East Asian cultures link it to confrontation.

discovery.text: Infants everywhere make eye contact. By age five, cultural rules reshape the habit.

twist.text: In parts of West Africa, children must look down when elders speak. Looking up means defiance.

climax.text: There's no universal honest gaze. Every culture coded eye contact to its own power structure.

punchline.text: Trust looks different depending on where you stand.

quiz.question: In many East Asian cultures, prolonged eye contact signals what?
